prompt: What kind of product forms when a conjugated diene undergoes a Diels–Alder reaction with an alkene?

choices.text: A substituted cyclohexene
A substituted cyclohexane
choices.why: The new ring keeps one double bond, formed between carbons 2 and 3 of the diene, so it is a cyclohexene.

choices.text: A substituted cyclopentene
choices.why: Four carbons from the diene plus two from the alkene make a six-membered ring.

choices.text: An open-chain triene
choices.why: The two reactants join into a ring. A cycloaddition gives a cyclic product.

explanation: Conjugated dienes undergo an addition reaction with alkenes to yield substituted cyclohexene products. For example, 1,3-butadiene and 3-buten-2-one give 3-cyclohexenyl methyl ketone.

prompt: How many new carbon–carbon single bonds form in one Diels–Alder reaction?
explanation: The Diels–Alder reaction forms two carbon–carbon bonds in a single step: the two alkene carbons bond to carbons 1 and 4 of the diene. Forming a ring this way is why the reaction is so useful.

prompt: How is the mechanism of the Diels–Alder reaction classified?

choices.text: Pericyclic: one step, with a cyclic redistribution of bonding electrons
Polar: an electrophile adds to give a carbocation, then a nucleophile bonds
choices.why: The Diels–Alder reaction is neither polar nor radical; no carbocation intermediate forms.

choices.text: Radical: a chain reaction with initiation, propagation and termination steps
choices.why: No radicals are involved. The reaction is a pericyclic process.

choices.text: Pericyclic: two steps, with one new C–C bond formed in each
choices.why: Both new C–C bonds form at the same time, in a single step through a cyclic transition state.

explanation: The Diels–Alder mechanism is neither polar nor radical. It is a pericyclic process: the two reactants join in a single step through a cyclic transition state in which the two new C–C bonds form at the same time.

choices.text: A reaction in which two reactants add together to give a cyclic product
A reaction in which a ring opens to give an open-chain product
choices.why: That's the reverse. In a cycloaddition, two reactants join to form a ring.

choices.text: A reaction in which one molecule forms a ring by losing a small molecule
choices.why: A cycloaddition joins two reactants, and nothing is lost.

choices.text: Any addition of HX or X2 to a cycloalkene
choices.why: Adding to an existing ring isn't the point. A cycloaddition creates a new ring from two reactants.

explanation: As the name implies, a cycloaddition reaction is one in which two reactants add together to give a cyclic product. The Diels–Alder reaction is one of the few general methods available for making cyclic molecules.

prompt: In the Diels–Alder transition state, how many carbon atoms rehybridize from sp2 to sp3?
explanation: The two alkene carbons and carbons 1 and 4 of the diene, four carbons in all, rehybridize from sp2 to sp3 to form the two new single bonds. Carbons 2 and 3 of the diene stay sp2 and form the new double bond.

prompt: What happens to carbons 2 and 3 of the diene during a Diels–Alder reaction?

choices.text: They stay sp2-hybridized and form the new double bond of the cyclohexene
They become sp3 and form the two new single bonds to the alkene
choices.why: Carbons 1 and 4 of the diene form the new single bonds to the two alkene carbons.

choices.text: They become sp-hybridized and form a triple bond
choices.why: They remain sp2; the former single bond between them becomes a double bond.

choices.text: Nothing: the single bond between them stays a single bond
choices.why: Both original double bonds of the diene are used up, and a new double bond forms between carbons 2 and 3.

explanation: In the transition state, the two alkene carbons and carbons 1 and 4 of the diene rehybridize from sp2 to sp3, while carbons 2 and 3 of the diene remain sp2-hybridized to form the new double bond in the cyclohexene product.

prompt: 1,3-Butadiene and ethylene have three π bonds between them. How many π bonds does their Diels–Alder product, cyclohexene, have?
explanation: Cyclohexene has one double bond, between the former carbons 2 and 3 of the diene. The other π electrons have gone into the two new C–C single bonds that close the ring.

prompt: Why is the Diels–Alder reaction so useful in the laboratory?

choices.text: It forms two C–C bonds in one step and is one of the few general ways to make rings
It converts conjugated dienes into nonconjugated dienes in one step
choices.why: The product is a cyclohexene with one double bond, not a diene.

choices.text: It adds H and Br across carbons 1 and 4 of a conjugated diene
choices.why: That is 1,4-addition of HBr. The Diels–Alder reaction joins a diene and an alkene into a ring.

choices.text: It opens rings to give long, unbranched carbon chains
choices.why: It does the reverse, building a six-membered ring from two reactants.

explanation: The Diels–Alder cycloaddition is extremely useful because it forms two carbon–carbon bonds in a single step and is one of the few general methods available for making cyclic molecules. Otto Diels and Kurt Alder received the 1950 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for its discovery.

prompt: How can the bond formation in a Diels–Alder reaction be pictured?

choices.text: Head-on (σ) overlap of the two alkene p orbitals with the p orbitals on carbons 1 and 4 of the diene
Head-on (σ) overlap of the two alkene p orbitals with the p orbitals on carbons 2 and 3 of the diene
choices.why: Carbons 2 and 3 form the new double bond. The new σ bonds go to carbons 1 and 4, the ends of the diene.

choices.text: Sideways (π) overlap of the two alkene p orbitals with the p orbitals on carbons 1 and 4 of the diene
choices.why: The two new bonds are σ single bonds, which form by head-on overlap.

choices.text: Sideways (π) overlap of the two alkene p orbitals with the p orbitals on carbons 2 and 3 of the diene
choices.why: The new bonds form at the ends of the diene, carbons 1 and 4, by head-on σ overlap.

explanation: We can picture a Diels–Alder addition as head-on (σ) overlap of the two alkene p orbitals with the two p orbitals on carbons 1 and 4 of the diene, a cyclic orientation of the reactants (Figure 14.4.1).

prompt: 1,3-Butadiene reacts with 3-buten-2-one (H2C=CHCOCH3) in a Diels–Alder reaction. What is the product?

choices.text: 3-Cyclohexenyl methyl ketone
1-Cyclohexenyl methyl ketone
choices.why: The acetyl group stays on a former alkene carbon, which becomes sp3. The new double bond forms between the diene's carbons 2 and 3, away from that carbon.

choices.text: 2-Cyclohexenyl methyl ketone
choices.why: The ring carbon with the acetyl group is bonded to carbon 1 of the diene, which becomes sp3, so the double bond starts one carbon farther away.

choices.text: Cyclohexyl methyl ketone
choices.why: The product keeps one ring double bond, between the former carbons 2 and 3 of the diene.

explanation: The alkene carbons bond to carbons 1 and 4 of the diene, and a new double bond forms between the diene's carbons 2 and 3. The ring carbon bearing the acetyl group is separated from the double bond by one CH2, giving 3-cyclohexenyl methyl ketone (96% in the section's example).
